pr_title: Add an error dialog when we fail to parse settings
pr_body:
## Summary of the Pull Request
Add an error dialog when we fail to parse settings. 

## PR Checklist
* [x] Closes #622 
* [x] CLA signed. If not, go over [here](https://cla.opensource.microsoft.com/microsoft/Terminal) and sign the CLA
* [x] Tested manually. 
* [x] I've discussed this with core contributors already. 

## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments
Sneak peek:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18356694/58040776-f3f7e400-7afb-11e9-804a-656defc238c1.png)
* If we fail to load the settings, we'll temporarily use the default settings. These defaults won't get written back to the profiles.json file, so people don't need to worry about blowing their settings away with a simple typo.
* This includes a bit of a XAML hack to make the button appear correctly when the app's theme is opposite that of the system theme. `ContentDialog` does a weird thing where it takes its child and moves that to the popup and leaves itself in the tree. That causes things like `ElementTheme` inheritance to break. So instead, we're theming the `CloseButton` manually, to make sure it's always visible.

issue_context.title: There should be an error dialog for incorrect settings instead of just crashing
issue_context.body:
Windows Build: 10.0.18362.86

Open Terminal.

Opened up settings, to profiles.json.

On a profile, for example cmd, added `"icon": %windir%\\system32\\cmd.exe`. Save.

On trying to focus on the terminal, it crashed. No errors. Almost instant crash.

Removed that line.

Tries to relaunch terminal, unable to launch it again.
Tried rebooting. Tried redeploying, did not work.

Edit: nvm, was just an extra comma in the end. It would launch again. But crashes when that exe is there.
i feel stupid for posting this issue without a second thought.
comments:
Yea there's no way for us to get an image from an .exe at this time.

I'd recommend trying a .png, .jpg, or any other image format :)
I am gonna take this issue as an opportunity to create a "there should be an error dialog for incorrect settings instead of just crashing" thread.
Just noting, that the json files gets resaved as unformatted json when you use the app. Making it difficult to change your settings at the go.

Windows Terminal crashed after I upgraded powershell-core from a old version to 7.0.0-preview.1.
This may because it cannot find the main shell. But I think it's better to "fall back" to cmd.

review_comments:
This decoupling worries me. It's because we need to cache the value to handle it later in `OnLoaded`?
Is there a better way to do that?
Yea. I could probably just have _TryLoadSEttings return the HRESULT, and then set the value on the other side of the call.
I'm only 50% on whether we should be writing the settings out on load honestly

As a use case for writing back out - people would need to delete their profiles.json file to get the app to write out the file including keybindings once that PR is in. Otherwise they'd have to add all the keybindings manually.
That's true ... but also, we might want to document it as a stopgap that is only necessary while we don't have a settings UI or some sort of "save my settings" functionality

An alternative solution might be to to write an example profile to the directory without modifying the user's profile except when it has actually changed.

Another alternative might be that once a json library is in use that supports comments, properties that haven't changed from the current default value could be saved commented, while ones explicitly changed by the user would actually be written out.

Regardless though, always modifying the configuration file when unnecessary is unfortunate.
I like the idea of dumping an example.
This seems like a discussion that's maybe better off in #754
#721, method capitalization needs to be changed.
